title: American Convention on Human Rights Article 1 — State Obligation to Respect and Ensure Convention Rights Without Discrimination
category: International Aviation / Human Rights / Treaty Law
allegation_summary: Article 1(1) of the ACHR is the Convention's foundational obligation: States Parties undertake to 'respect the rights and freedoms recognized herein and to ensure to all persons subject to their jurisdiction the free and full exercise of those rights and freedoms, without any discrimination.' This obligation has two dimensions: a negative obligation (to respect — i.e., not to violate) and a positive obligation (to ensure — i.e., to prevent violations and provide effective remedies). Chile, through its agents (DGAC and PDI), violated the negative obligation by directly participating in acts that infringed the passenger's Article 5 (humane treatment), Article 7 (personal liberty), and Article 8 (due process) rights. Chile violated the positive obligation by failing to maintain a regulatory framework that would prevent private actors (LATAM) from violating Convention rights, by failing to investigate the violations, and by failing to provide an effective remedy.

articles.article_text: The States Parties to this Convention undertake to respect the rights and freedoms recognized herein and to ensure to all persons subject to their jurisdiction the free and full exercise of those rights and freedoms, without any discrimination for reasons of race, color, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, economic status, birth, or any other social condition.
